subject.title: Expose maxMissedJobsPerRestart and missedJobStaggerMs in cron config

question: Should OpenClaw expose restart catch-up controls in public cron config, and if so should the supported shape be the existing global max/stagger knobs, a skip/catch-up policy, or no new public config?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the root policy treats new config/default surfaces as compatibility-sensitive and the choice changes restart semantics for existing scheduled jobs.

options.title: Expose narrow global controls
options.body: Approve a documented global cron restart catch-up policy using the existing internal max/stagger behavior, including explicit disable semantics for a zero immediate limit.

options.title: Prefer skip policy instead
options.body: Design a global or per-job skipMissedRuns-style policy before implementation, preserving current catch-up defaults for existing users.

options.title: Keep controls internal
options.body: Decline new public config and keep the current fixed restart catch-up defaults while documenting the behavior and workarounds.

recommendation.title: Expose narrow global controls
recommendation.body: Approve a documented global cron restart catch-up policy using the existing internal max/stagger behavior, including explicit disable semantics for a zero immediate limit.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a public config and scheduler-semantics decision; steipete landed the internal restart catch-up change and appears in adjacent config/cron history.
